walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
A group of words from a similar area of meaning — e.g. 'whisper, scream, mumble, shout' all belong to the semantic field of vocalisation.
A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
Meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said — generated when speakers obey or deliberately flout Grice's maxims. 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all', via the maxim of quantity.
Implicature is the same as the literal meaning of a sentence.
